slides.heading: Check in first if you

caption:
Every time the bridge gets hard, Momo holds her breath. Afterwards her neck feels it more than her tummy.

Most people hold their breath when a movement gets tough. It often adds tension through the neck and jaw and makes control harder. A simple starting point: breathe in to prepare, breathe out through the hardest part. A slow out-breath helps you feel the deep tummy and pelvic floor muscles switch on.

Hybi's 1-minute rib breathing: lie down, knees bent, hands on your lower ribs. In through the nose for four, out through the mouth for six. Five rounds before bed.

The clinical Pilates team at Hybrid Physio starts with a one-on-one assessment and coaches breathing into every exercise. Book online via the link in bio 🐱
